title: Savoy residents famous as new water system is completed
publication: The Bonham Daily Favorite, Bonham, Texas
text:
THE BONHAM DAILY FAVORITE — Bonham, Texas — Friday, Feb. 27, 1987 — Page 6

Savoy residents famous as new water system is completed

By EULA PHILLIPS
Savoy Correspondent

SAVOY — The city of Savoy has long suffered the inconvenience of a water system in need of repair, and the lack of funds to conduct exploratory work. Much of the deterioration in the system was attributed to high water consumption that would surely result in a conservation order from the Texas Department of Health, absence of storage facilities and an inadequate water distribution system throughout the city.

In January 1987, the governing body, consisting of Mayor Arlester Jackson, City Secretary Khanell[?], and three council members, Claudia Jones set in motion a plan to secure a new water system for the people of Savoy.

The first requirement was to hire an engineering firm. Assistance in obtaining funding for the project from a community development fund was made available when the Engineering Company of Austin was retained. A resolution was passed to secure a loan from the Texas Water Development Board.

The next requirement was to hire a contractor. Three competitive bids were taken and the Texhoma Contractors of Lubbock was selected.

The report was completed and submitted to the city in August 1985. The next step was for the council to follow a direct program as required to meet the standards. The Texas Water Development Board approved the city's application as a priority project.

The full line was completed in September 1985.

Savoy's officials, including Mayor Jackson and city secretary, attended a public meeting held in May 1985 at the Texas Water Development Board offices in Austin, and were requested to submit a detailed financial needs assessment.

The Texas Water Development Board (TWDB) reduced the cost of the project because of the additional cost of the new meters. The TWDB noted that the total cost of the project was $358,000. The TWDB reduced the loan to allow for the $53,000 TDCA grant of $53,000, to be used for reducing the cost of the project, in September 1985.

The full loan was completed in September 1985.

Savoy's citizens, including 160 those that have bought the water, have also celebrated this with various civic and domestic commitments.

The old threat of the city's water was completely replaced including 16,000 feet of new water lines, and almost all 160 old connections have been replaced — two six-inch lines, one eight-inch line, three two-inch lines, and ten one-inch lines.

Water pressure on the far western end of the system was helped substantially. Well new water transmission lines — as well as new sewer lines — will be added to the water service. Also smaller water mains were replaced with larger ones. Water storage was enhanced. "All the water wasn't reaching the people," said Mayor Jackson. "We didn't have adequate pressure."

The old threat of the city's water system was gradually replaced including new meters.

A new mayor was elected, Brad Jackson, who succeeds Mayor Arlester Jackson, and three new council members were elected replacing Jimmy Deptord and Richell Upshaw. Upshaw had been assigned to water. Upshaw had resigned to run an unannounced race for the mayor's seat.

Mayor Jackson, who continues to serve as city secretary, also said the office staff has been reduced — there is no longer a full-time city secretary. She said the city would consult outside counsel as needed.

Old elected city administrators were being advised that it was a mistake to continue with water, and the board tried to interfere with the new system's plans.

The old council members of this growing community were eager to do the best for the growing needs of the school, and the city administrators, old and new, were doing their best in the early period of the project.
